title: Pergamum (Revelation 2:12–17)
hookLine: a white stone with a new name only you know

cards: A small white stone. That's the gift at the end of today's letter, and the letter never says what it means. It goes to the church in Pergamum, a city the King James spells Pergamos.
The risen Christ speaks as the one with the sharp sword with two edges, and his first words aren't a complaint. He knows their address: "where Satan's seat is." A hard place to live.
Then, at the very end, the strange promise: a white stone, with a new name only the one who receives it knows.

teach.h: HOLDING FAST WHERE SATAN'S SEAT IS.
teach.b: First, where they lived. They "holdest fast my name, and hast not denied my faith." The letter names one man, Antipas, "my faithful martyr, who was slain among you."
That's all the text says about him. What Satan's seat was, it doesn't say either. Some readers point to the city's great altars and temples; others to the worship of the emperor.
Second, the trouble. Not everyone held the same line. The letter warns about some who held the teaching of Balaam, the hired prophet from Numbers, and others who held the teaching of the Nicolaitans.
Faithful under pressure from outside, still muddled inside, and the letter says both.

teach.h: HIDDEN MANNA AND A WHITE STONE.
teach.b: Third, the promise: "To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it."

Hidden manna reaches back to the bread in the wilderness. The white stone, readers have guessed at: a white pebble a juror cast to acquit, or a token that let a guest into a feast. The text doesn't explain.

teach.h: A NEW NAME ONLY ONE PERSON KNOWS.
teach.b: Fourth, the name. In the Bible, people are renamed at turning points: Abram becomes Abraham, Jacob becomes Israel, and Jesus calls Simon Peter. Here the new name isn't announced to the crowd.
It's written on a stone and known only to the one who holds it. Others may know someone by a job, a reputation, a worst day. This letter says there's a name none of them gets to read.

how: Christians read the seven letters of Revelation 2–3 both as messages to real early churches and as words for churches today, and Bible study groups sometimes take them one letter at a time.

games.q: you're in the church at Pergamum. you live where Satan's seat is, and a man named Antipas has been killed. what does the letter say about you?
o: you have denied the faith to stay safe.
you hold fast the name and have not denied the faith.
you have left your first love.
games.why: "thou holdest fast my name, and hast not denied my faith." faithful outside, and still warned about the muddle inside.

practice: Hold a small stone, or anything small and plain, in your palm, and feel its weight and edges as it warms.
Let a question rest there without answering it in words: what would be written on it by someone who knew you all the way through, not your title, not your mistakes?
If you pray, hold it and simply listen; if not, just hold it, and breathe.

wordCard.voice: Pergamum. A church holding fast in a hard place, warned about its muddle, and promised hidden manna and a white stone with a new name.

orig.note: Greek: a small stone, a pebble. the white stone of Revelation 2:17.

carryVoice: Your line: a new name. Written on a stone that nobody else gets to read. Until tomorrow.
